Key findings: A weighted donor pool reproduces the treated unit's counterfactual path; credibility rests on pre-period fit.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C2: why EU-wide events leave no foreign comparator.

Study design, data and period: Methodological review of synthetic-control designs; no single study period.
Method: Weighted donor counterfactual; assessment of fit and donor suitability.
Key findings: Explains when synthetic controls are credible and when poor fit, unsuitable donors or interference undermine them.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C2: comparator feasibility and limits to causal attribution.

Study design, data and period: Sweden versus OECD donor pool; transport CO₂.
Key findings: Transport CO₂ fell almost 11% after the carbon tax and fuel VAT, mostly due to the tax; single-sector, CO₂-only.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C2: exemplar single-country ex post evaluation.

Study design, data and period: Implementation review of LMDI formulations; energy and emissions applications.
Method: Comparison of decomposition formulae and implementation choices.
Key findings: Guidance on choosing and implementing LMDI; factorisation determines interpretation.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2; C3: consistent accounting of component effects.

Study design, data and period: Methodological development with energy-related CO₂ applications.
Method: Additive and multiplicative log-mean Divisia decomposition.
Key findings: Residual-free decomposition with aggregation consistency; accounting contributions are not policy effects.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2; C3: exact scale–intensity decomposition.

Study design, data and period: Qualitative Irish environmental-policy study; 34 stakeholder interviews.
Method: Interview-based analysis of perceived implementation barriers.
Key findings: Identifies capacity, incoherence, finance, political priorities and planning delays; not an agricultural impact estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3–RQ4; C1: implementation mechanisms and alternative explanations for weak mitigation.

Study design, data and period: Methodological study with simulations and illustrative series.
Method: Multiple-break estimation, break-date intervals, tests of break number.
Key findings: Practical procedures for detecting structural change under general error structures.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1; C2: regime detection and timing uncertainty.

Study design, data and period: National Farm Survey cross-section; 296 Irish dairy farms, 2015.
Method: Propensity-score matching of milk-recording adopters and non-adopters.
Key findings: Higher yield, margins and animal-health indicators without improved measured GHG efficiency; unobserved selection remains.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2, RQ4; C3: separates productivity benefits from assumed mitigation.

Study design, data and period: Critical appraisal of successive Irish agri-food strategies.
Method: Policy and sustainability synthesis; no causal estimator.
Key findings: Efficiency-led expansion did not reconcile growth with environmental pressures; policy largely reactive.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: production–mitigation tension and mixed strategic goals.

Study design, data and period: Review and synthesis of three meta-analyses; EU.
Key findings: Schemes raise farmland biodiversity on average; effects depend on design and landscape; post-2007 schemes no more effective.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C1: evidence base for voluntary agri-environment schemes.

Study design, data and period: Econometric methods paper (NBER Working Paper No. 32117).
Key findings: Identification conditions and estimands for continuous-dose DiD.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C2: continuous-exposure regional design.

Key findings: Integration is a process; frames, subsystems, goals and instruments can move at different speeds or in opposite directions.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: incoherence as time-varying.

Key findings: Agriculture not on track; projected to exceed its 2030 ceiling with existing measures.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: accountability context and 2030 ceiling.

Author(s) and year: Climate Action and Low Carbon Development (Amendment) Act 2021
Study design, data and period: Irish statute, No. 32 of 2021; legal rather than empirical evidence.
Method: Statutory provisions on carbon budgets and sectoral ceilings.
Key findings: Creates a framework for national climate accountability; does not estimate abatement or cap individual farms.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: legal strength and targets versus instruments.

Method: Emission accounting along the food chain.
Key findings: Food systems produced about a third of global GHG emissions.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: global context for agriculture's role.

Study design, data and period: Irish National Farm Survey panel over 23 years; REPS, AEOS and GLAS.
Method: Random-effects logit models of scheme participation.
Key findings: Participant profiles vary; intensive-farm pressures insufficiently targeted; no national GHG estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C1: eligibility, selection and effective coverage.

Key findings: Target of 50% growth in milk production by 2020.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1, RQ3; C1: strategy signal G01.

Key findings: Targets of 65% growth in primary output value and 85% in exports.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: strategy signal G02.

Key findings: Growth goals with at least 10% biogenic-methane and over 50% fertiliser-emission reduction aims.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: mixed-goal strategy G03 (content weight 0.5).

Key findings: Combines sustainability with commercial and export ambitions; goals alone do not establish effects.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: cautious classification of mixed strategies.

Key findings: Technological progress cut emissions; affluence and population growth raised them.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2; C3: livestock application of LMDI.

Key findings: Layered reforms were durable; greening legitimised decoupled payments while income support persisted.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: empirical layering in agricultural policy.

Key findings: Output- and input-linked payments most harmful; decoupled payments least harmful.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: scoring expansion instruments.

Key findings: Sets agriculture's 2030 reduction at 25% relative to 2018, an absolute-sector ambition.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: absolute benchmark and event marker E02.

Study design, data and period: Irish agricultural-sector scenarios for Food Harvest 2020; conference paper.
Method: Partial-equilibrium modelling of activity and GHG emissions.
Key findings: Tensions between growth and emissions commitments; conditional on scenario assumptions.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C3: prospective evidence and the historical attribution gap.

Method: Legal documentation of Ireland's nitrates derogation and conditions.
Key findings: Permits higher manure-nitrogen applications on qualifying grassland farms; no GHG estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3–RQ4; C1: conditional relaxation of a limit (P03).

Study design, data and period: EU performance audit of climate-related CAP spending, 2014–2020.
Method: Audit of spending, design and mitigation potential.
Key findings: Over €100 billion attributed to climate; emissions not falling since 2010; funded practices often low-potential; not a scheme-level causal estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3–RQ4; C1: targeting and limits of expenditure measures.

Key findings: Enteric fermentation about 49%, soils 30%, manure 17%; non-CO₂ emissions down 6–7% since 2005.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: EU source structure for CH₄ and N₂O.

Study design, data and period: EU and Member State inventory synthesis, 1990–2024; Report 09/2026.
Method: Source- and gas-specific analysis of drivers.
Key findings: Slower reductions recently; milk growth partly offsets methane-intensity gains.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1–RQ2; C3: scale–intensity mechanism.

Method: Comparison of absolute and intensity caps under uncertainty.
Key findings: The two coincide only when future output is known.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2; C3: intensity versus absolute targets.

Key findings: Agriculture 37.9% of national emissions in 2024 under a definition that includes agricultural fuel.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1–RQ3: context and boundary consistency.

Method: Panel estimation of short- and longer-run legislative effects.
Key findings: Climate laws associated with lower CO₂ intensity; weaker for other gases.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1–C2: transfer limits for agricultural CH₄/N₂O.

Key findings: Livestock emissions fall mainly via lower output; leakage up to 91%.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3: hard-to-abate argument; ex ante modelling.

Key findings: Insufficient evidence to judge national environmental effectiveness.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C1: mitigation instrument M01 and evidence gap.

Key findings: Emissions per cow rise with yield; emissions per kg milk fall.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2; C3: productivity–intensity mechanism.

Key findings: Lower effective costs can induce demand; size depends on scope and context.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2–RQ3: analogy for the intensity offset.

Key findings: Voluntary schemes show limited impact, low uptake and scant outcome evidence.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C1: voluntary versus binding instruments.

Key findings: Market price support and unconstrained input payments most harmful; decoupled least.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: scoring expansion instruments.

Key findings: Economic potential under 10% of technical potential.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3: limits to assumed abatement.

Key findings: Yield gains with integrated markets could raise cropland and CO₂.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: rebound analogue in agriculture.

Key findings: Carbon pricing cuts EU emissions; leakage offsets part; trade liberalisation adds leakage.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3: limits of sector models.

Key findings: Mixes classified by number of goals, instruments and governance levels.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: policy-mix framing of M and P.

Key findings: Inherited instruments and incremental additions can create inconsistent portfolios.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: layering as a mechanism for conflicting incentives.

Key findings: Practice meets only some theoretical standards.
Relevance to the present study: Rationale for ex post evaluation.

Method: Assessment of inventories and mitigation literature.
Key findings: Agricultural CH₄ and N₂O about 6 Gt CO₂e a year; adoption conditions constrain abatement.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2–RQ3: emissions mechanisms.

Key findings: Removal cuts EU emissions; about three quarters offset by leakage.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: expansion instrument effects (P01).

Key findings: Post-quota supply inelastic; few member states expanded herds; short post-quota window.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1, RQ4: mixed evidence on abolition.

Method: Agnostic break detection with policy attribution.
Key findings: Ten successful interventions; best mixes combine fuel taxes with vehicle incentives.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1; C2: policy-as-break logic.

Key findings: Identifies measures towards the ceiling; stresses the scale of the challenge.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3: 2030 ceiling context.

Method: Control-function productivity; FE and dynamic-panel models.
Key findings: Productivity negatively associated with GHG intensity; total farm emissions rose; not a national abolition effect.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2, RQ4; C3: farm-scale mechanism.

Method: Comparison of designs with different biases.
Key findings: Convergence is more informative when biases differ.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1–RQ4; C2: triangulation rationale.

Key findings: No mandatory agricultural carbon price anywhere; intensity gains may not cut absolute emissions.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2–RQ3: hard-to-abate; intensity versus absolute.

Study design, data and period: ITS tutorial with a public-health application.
Key findings: Threats from concurrent interventions and misspecified trends.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1; C2: temporal identification.

Key findings: Robust conclusions need several lines of evidence.
Relevance to the present study: C2: triangulation rationale.

Key findings: AFOLU 13–21% of global emissions; enteric CH₄ main source.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: global CH₄ and N₂O context.

Key findings: Coherent goals can coexist with conflicting instruments; no offset estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: objectives versus operational interactions.

Key findings: Mean footprint 1.11 kg CO₂e per kg FPCM.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: low-intensity system context.

Key findings: Market, food-security and leakage trade-offs under specified assumptions.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3: scenarios versus realised effects.

Method: Comparative monitoring of support and targets.
Key findings: Commodity-linked support encourages production; many mitigation targets non-binding.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3–RQ4; C1: coverage and bindingness.

Key findings: Comparable scores do not establish comparable causal effects.
Relevance to the present study: C1; RQ3: transparent policy scoring.

Key findings: CAP failing on climate, biodiversity and soils; low-ambition options remain.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3: weak EU mitigation.

Method: Bounds testing in a conditional error-correction framework.
Key findings: Allows I(0)/I(1) regressors; excludes I(2); does not prove exogeneity.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C2: dynamic specification.

Key findings: Efficient irrigation increased groundwater extraction.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: empirical rebound in agriculture.

Key findings: Transport emissions fell; no large aggregate fall.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1, RQ3: outcome-dependence of results.

Method: Partial identification under restricted trend violations.
Key findings: Plausible violations can change causal conclusions.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C2: credibility of regional comparisons.

Method: Case-based assessment of options and barriers.
Key findings: Incoherent climate, agricultural and land-use policies obstruct mitigation; boundary extends beyond CRF3.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: agricultural coherence application.

Key findings: Consistency, credibility and processes shape mix performance; no offset estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: interacting instruments.

Study design, data and period: Conceptual paper applied to EU climate policy.
Key findings: Typology useful; empirical gaps on governing evaluation.
Relevance to the present study: Rationale for ex post evaluation.

Key findings: Backfire evidence inconclusive; economy-wide rebound may be larger than assumed.
Relevance to the present study: RQ2: rebound analogy.

Key findings: 63 interventions with large CO₂ reductions; pricing central in effective mixes.
Relevance to the present study: RQ1, RQ3; C2: sectoral transfer limits.

Key findings: Limited convergence with EU ambitions; does not isolate agricultural effects.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: governance context.

Key findings: N₂O about 6% lower by 2008; modelled co-benefit, not an Irish causal estimate.
Relevance to the present study: RQ4; C1: binding non-climate regulation (M02).

Key findings: Quantifies declared priorities and leakage risk; not realised offsets.
Relevance to the present study: RQ3; C1: closest quantitative coherence precedent.
